text:
alyssa: Quick follow-up from last night's outage — TLS handshakes failed intermittently for cross-region traffic hitting the east->eu LB. Postmortem notes say a config push introduced an SNI fallback edge-case. I want to track owners/timeline for the fixes and prevent recurrence.

mario: saw the spike in `TLS handshake error: alert handshake failure` in the logs around 02:14 UTC. retries caused connection bursts to fallback pool. :eyes:

jia: confirm it's the SNI fallback. I reproduced locally with curl and a VM that strips SNI: `curl --resolve lb.redwood.test:443:10.0.0.5 https://lb.redwood.test/` -> handshake fails, server falls back and we see routing `503` from fallback path.

ops-lead: assignables: (1) roll back unsafe SNI fallback logic in routing layer, (2) add canary + traffic fencing for LB config pushes, (3) detection alert for SNI-mismatch-induced retries.

alyssa: suggested owners? mario take (1) and (3)? jia take (2) can you own canary policy + playbook update?

mario: I can own (1) and (3). ETA for code fix and rollout: EOD tomorrow Pacific. I'll open a PR and tag for expedited review.

jia: I'll own the canary + playbook. Plan: create a `lb-config-canary` route with 1% traffic, test SNI variations, and add a pre-deploy checklist that includes `curl` SNI test and `openssl s_client` validation. ETA 3 business days.

sre-oncall: I'll add a temporary monitor to detect hallmark pattern: increased TLS handshake failures + cross-region routing hops + elevated retries in the LB proxy logs. Put it as Pager when failures > 50 in 5m.

incident-bot: incident 2026-06-04T02:14Z created. Severity: P2. Postmortem draft available at https://redwood.internal/pm/2026-06-lb-tls-sni

ops-lead: action items and owners summary: - mario: revert fallback logic PR + tests (due 2026-06-05 EOD) - jia: add canary + deploy playbook updates (due 2026-06-09) - sre-oncall: detection alert + dashboard (due 2026-06-06) - alyssa: verify downstream customers and coordinate comms (due 2026-06-07)

mario: opening PR now: https://git.redwood/s/repo/pulls/1425 — includes unit tests and an integration scenario. Requesting fast-track review from @jia and @ops-lead.

jia: ack, will review in the morning. For the canary I'll add a `lb-config.canary: true` flag and a circuit breaker for SNI mismatch so we can disable the fallback per region quickly.

alyssa: good. also let's log the exact headers in a safe way (no cert material) for post-incident analysis. mario please add a debug flag gated behind `DEBUG_LB_HANDSHAKE=true` for short-lived runs.

mario: will do. adding to PR. Also adding a small script in `/infra/tools/verify_sni.sh` for CI:```#!/bin/bash
set -e
HOST=$1
openssl s_client -servername $HOST -connect $HOST:443 </dev/null | head -n 20
```

ops-lead: can we add a synthetic that runs across regions every 10m to assert TLS handshake + SNI behavior? put in /observability/synthetics and make results visible in console.

sre-oncall: yes. I'll add synthetic with tags `sni`, `cross-region`, alert on >2 failures in 6 checks.

alyssa: quick note on recurrence: this looks like the same symptom pattern as the Jan incident (sni-mismatch + retries) but different root cause. Let's add a short section in the PM about recurring incident class and recommended guardrails (canary, automatic rollback for TLS regressions).

mario: will include a "recurrence" section in the PR description and link to Jan postmortem.

ops-lead: closing loop: please put concrete verification steps in the postmortem and update the runbook `runbooks/lb-tls-issues.md` with a step-by-step rollback and canary ramp commands. We'll reconvene 2026-06-07 14:00 UTC for status.

jia: scheduling calendar invite and will add agenda: PR review, canary config, synthetic watchdog.

alyssa: thanks team. tagging this thread as the canonical follow-up. ping if any slips on ETA so we can escalate. :thumbsup:
